title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-24
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent failures and huge latency spikes observed when serving long-context requests around certain sequence-length thresholds (observed at 1024, 2048).
- Symptoms: kv-cache index OOB assertions, sudden kernel fallback to slower attention implementation, and token generation latency jump (~10-120ms per token).
- Reproducible locally with model gptz-13b-8bit and the test harness (see repro steps).

Reproduction (minimal):
1) Start runtime with debug logging and kernel override off:
   ./bin/serve --model gptz-13b --quantize int8 --port 4200 --log-level debug
2) Run requester (single stream, keep-alive):
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4200/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"A"*N, "max_new_tokens":256}'
   where N ~= 1800..2100 to hit the edge region.
3) Alternately run unit harness that directly exercises KV cache:
   python tests/kv_cache/seqlen_repro.py --seqlen 2049 --warmup 10

Observed errors / logs (snippets):
- runtime log (trace):
  [2024-11-18 14:03:22.128] ERROR runtime/kv_cache.cpp:142 Assertion failed: kv_index < kv_capacity (pos=2049, cap=2048)
- attention kernel selection debug output:
  [DEBUG] kernel_selector: chosen=fast_mha (optimized)
  [DEBUG] kernel_selector: fallback=distributed_mha (latency heavy) -- triggered when seq_len > 2048 and memory layout != tiled
- client-side latency trace (single request):
  token 1..2048 => median 11ms
  token 2049.. => median 118ms (and occasional OOM or assertion)

Commands tried / hacks attempted so far:
- Force kernel preference env var:
  export RW_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=fast_mha
  // result: runtime still falls back after allocating KV buffer; no assert but severe slowdown
- Increase KV capacity pre-alloc:
  ./bin/serve --kv-capacity 4096 --model gptz-13b
  // result: suppresses assertion but latency spike persists; memory usage grows predictably
- Toggle caching off for long requests:
  POST body: {"cache":false} => avoids OOB but increases compute (higher latency than normal but stable)
- Try older kernel selection code (git checkout commit 1a2b3c):
  // result: less aggressive fallback, fewer fallbacks but wrong attention results for >2048 due to earlier bug fixed in current main
- Reproduced with quantized and float weights; behavior exists in both but more severe with int8 due to packing differences

Hypotheses / notes:
- Off-by-one in KV indexing when switching kernel/backing buffer layout at threshold boundaries (e.g., runtime switches to tiled KV layout at multiples of 1024 and fails to update index mapping).
- Kernel selector policy uses sequence-length buckets (<=1024, <=2048, >2048). Boundary condition at 2048 may not update stride/packing metadata.
- Quantization packing changes alignment so the tiled buffer stride calculation differs and exposes the bug faster.
- Fallback path to distributed_mha triggers a re-binding of KV storage without updating the "head_offset" used by attention kernel, producing OOB accesses.

Quick experiments to validate hypothesis:
- Add extra logging in kernel_selector::choose() to print current kv_layout, kv_capacity, head_offset before and after selection (done locally; shows head_offset stale after selection).
- Re-run repro after instrumenting kv_cache::reserve() to always zero-initialize new KV memory. When zeroed, assertions sometimes convert to wrong outputs rather than OOB (suggests stale metadata).
- Insert a small guard in kv_cache::get_index(pos): if pos >= kv_capacity then clamp and log; this prevents assert but downstream correctness unknown.

Notes on kernel selection behavior:
- kernel_selector currently uses config thresholds (kernel_buckets = [1024,2048,4096]) in runtime/config.cpp
- Some code paths override based on model.arch (gptz has patch to prefer tiled_mha) and on hw (A100 prefers fast_mha).
- When request crosses threshold mid-stream (e.g., context accumulation grows past 2048 during generation), runtime attempts to migrate kernel/backing storage on-the-fly which is NOT atomic - race condition potential.

Test vectors tried (include seed / input shape):
- small seed: 1 token prompt, then generate until 2100 tokens (deterministic seed=42) -> reproduces reliably on dev machine
- warm prompt: 1500 token prompt + generate 800 -> sometimes reproduces depending on batch alignment
- batch size 4 vs 1: issue more frequent in batch>1 where different stream lengths cause per-stream KV layout mismatch

Immediate fixes considered (short-term):
- Disable on-the-fly kernel migration at runtime (config flag: runtime.allow_kernel_migration=false). Quick patch reduced incidents in smoke tests.
- Add atomic swap for backing KV buffer with metadata update under mutex. Slower but correct.
- Add unit tests: tests/kv_cache/test_seqlen_edgecases.py that exercise boundary at 1024/2048/4096 and mid-generation crossing.

Longer-term / refactor ideas:
- Unify KV layout abstraction so kernel backends never perform implicit re-layout; instead runtime always provides canonical view and kernels implement mapping.
- Move kernel selection decision to request start only; if we must migrate mid-request, do safe copy/transform with consistent metadata update and validation.
- Improve fuzz coverage in CI for sequence length growth patterns.

Next actions / TODOs (who/when):
- [Evan] Prototype disable-migration toggle and add to canary config (INF-1293) -> done locally, needs review, push PR (blocking: regression tests)
- [Priya] Add unit tests for boundary cases (tests/kv_cache/test_seqlen_edgecases.py) -> assigned, in progress
- [Lucas] Profile fallback kernel (distributed_mha) to see why latency is so high; check for extra memory operations -> asked to collect perf traces
- Create PR referencing this scratchpad: /serving-runtime PR #842 (draft)

Breadcrumbs / slack / meeting notes:
- Discussion thread: #serving-runtime on 2024-11-18 (link above) - flagged by SRE after Canary run 11/17
- Infra change INF-1293 created to track canaries and config toggles

Attachments / artifacts to include in PR:
- Reproducer harness: tests/kv_cache/seqlen_repro.py (local)
- Kernel selector logs: artifacts/kernel-logs-20241118.tar.gz (uploaded to internal S3)
- Perf traces: perf/fallback-distributed-mha-11-18.trace

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is on-the-fly migration ever required for customer workloads? If not, default to disable.
- Are there models for which tiled layout is always superior? Need matrix of model.arch x hw -> preferred_layout.
- Can we standardize kv_capacity growth policy to avoid mid-request reallocation?

If anyone else hits this - please add any new repro input shapes to this doc and tag me. I'll push the disable-migration RFC in the next PR and add the unit tests.

-- Evan
